attractions.name: Bolan Pass
attractions.description: A historic mountain pass connecting the Indus plains to the Balochistan highlands, used since ancient times and famous for its dramatic gorge scenery and colonial-era railway.

attractions.name: Bolan River Gorge
attractions.description: Dramatic rocky gorge scenery along the Bolan River, especially scenic along the historic railway route.

transportation.notes: Most common route to the provincial capital
Long-distance coach services connect to Karachi
Shared vans are the main local transport option

weather_info.climate_type: Mountain climate with mild summers and cold winters

seasonal_notes.avg_condition: Mild, 15-30°C, main visiting season for highland areas
Cold, often below freezing, occasional snow at higher elevations

travel_tips.tip: Check seasonal conditions before visiting Bolan — mountain districts can have snow-blocked roads in winter, desert districts are extremely hot in summer.
Intercity coaches and shared vans connect most district towns to Quetta; travel times can be long given Balochistan's size.
Check current local travel advisories before visiting, as conditions can vary across Balochistan's districts.

history.founded: Named after the historic Bolan Pass, a strategic mountain route since ancient times
history.city_history: Bolan District (historically Kachhi) contains the famous Bolan Pass, a strategic mountain corridor used by traders and armies for millennia, later developed by the British as a key rail and road route between Sindh and Quetta.
history.province_history: Balochistan is Pakistan's largest province by area and least populated, historically home to the Baloch and Pashtun peoples and the site of the ancient Mehrgarh civilization (one of the earliest farming settlements in South Asia). It was ruled by the Khanate of Kalat before acceding to Pakistan in 1948, and remains known for its vast deserts, mountain ranges, and long Arabian Sea coastline.
